reason: The cited evidence discusses general thermodynamic effects of mixing on melting point depression (E1) and the schematic relationship between heat capacity, configurational entropy, and solidus temperature (E2), but neither provides specific prior experimental validation of multiplexed DSC-dilatometry, CALPHAD screening accuracy for HEA melting, or the distinctness of melting signatures in single-phase HEAs. The key premises thus lack direct, specific prior support.
premises: CALPHAD can pre-screen HEA compositions to target single-phase solid solutions with measurable melting ranges
Multiplexed DSC can accurately measure melting temperature and latent heat for an array of HEA compositions
Simultaneous dilatometry or in-situ imaging can capture volume change at melting for these alloys
Single-phase solid-solution HEAs yield a single, well-defined melting event detectable by DSC
Configurational entropy stabilizes a uniform phase and distinct melting signature in HEAs
